summary: Digest-bound prerequisites for first native adoption

delivery.outcome: Complete the existing first-bootstrap prerequisite repair including directory-symlink race refusal and bounded regular-file plan reads, then deliver standard0.20.133 through full qualified checks, independent review/merge and canonical release; retain explicit CI prerequisites. Qualify the additional Goal-wide pytest collection and isolate the existing bridge fixture import without changing production status resolution.
nonGoals: No consumer edits, legacy owner takeover, arbitrary file creation, overwrite, policy weakening or default seeding.
No writer/publication authority in a seed plan or installer receipt; existing native allocation and independent approval remain mandatory.

architecture.decision: An optional bounded external closed JSON plan binds current target HEAD and literal content/digests for only absent required VERSION, CHANGELOG.md, TODO.md and project/TICKETS.md. Validate symlink/commit absence and reread before effects; create exclusively and include exact bytes in the existing bootstrap receipt. Existing first-allocation, ownership and independent protected publication guards remain unchanged. Pin external plan parent directories and target seed directories with no-follow directory descriptors, read at most the metadata limit plus one byte from a regular nonblocking file descriptor, create leaf seeds exclusively, and reject replaced parent/root bindings before managed writes. The opt-in seed mode refuses hosts without the required race-resistant descriptor operations before effects. Keep the existing legacy SQLite bridge test bound to its explicitly patched ticket_activity module during shared pytest collection, which also loads isolated activity fixtures. Preserve its successful-status and conflicting-status assertions.
interfaceChanges: Opt-in --bootstrap-prerequisites-plan for explicit first bootstrap only
dataChanges: Closed external new-project.bootstrap-prerequisites-plan/v1 plan; existing receipt format unchanged
Opt-in prerequisite plans require supported no-follow directory-descriptor operations; ordinary adoption modes retain their existing platform contract.
architecture.rollback: Protected revert; retain old immutable standard releases. Never use unreviewed candidate in actual consumer repositories.

commands: targeted bootstrap CLI and first-allocation regressions
validation.evidence: Successful read-only review, bounded seed installation and exact native first allocation; existing target bytes/foreign paths preserved.
Invalid or changed plans make no writes; default missing-prerequisite refusal unchanged.
No consumer use before independent source merge and actual canonical published0.20.133 release.
